definition: Robopsychology is the study of the personalities and behavior of intelligent machines.
details: The term was coined by Isaac Asimov in the short stories collected in I, Robot, which featured robopsychologist Dr. Susan Calvin, and whose plots largely revolved around the protagonist solving problems connected with intelligent robot behaviour. The term has been also used in some academic studies from the field of psychology and human–computer interactions, and it refers to the study of the psychological consequences of living in societies where the application of robotics is becoming increasingly common.

explainer.lead: Robopsychology is the study of the personalities and behavior of intelligent machines. It has also been used in academic psychology and human–computer interaction to describe the psychological consequences of living in societies where robotics is increasingly applied.

tiers.eli5: Like having a therapist whose patients are robots, and also studying how people feel living alongside them.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers use the term in psychology and human–computer interaction studies of how people respond to increasingly present robotics. Its fictional origin means the term spans both imagined machine minds and real human consequences.
tiers.paperLevel: The study of the personalities and behavior of intelligent machines; the term was coined by Isaac Asimov in the I, Robot stories.

explainer.example: An HCI study examining how people's psychology shifts as robots become common in daily life draws on the term.
